Thought: Alkynes are hydrocarbons that contain at least one carbon-carbon triple bond. The general formula for alkynes is CnH2n-2. They can have terminal or internal triple bonds. Terminal alkynes have the structure R-CC-H, which includes an acetylenic hydrogen (the hydrogen attached to the carbon of the triple bond). Internal alkynes have the structure R-CC-R, where both groups attached to the carbon atoms of the triple bond are organic residues (R), and no acetylenic hydrogen is present. The question asks for the structure of alkynes with no acetylenic hydrogen, indicating an internal alkyne. Therefore, the correct structure is R-CC-R.
